The processes come from get_context('spawn').Process, which is SpawnProcess, a subclass of BaseProcess and not of multiprocessing.Process. The check is therefore always False and kill() never runs. When the cause is 'hang', the stuck process stays alive and a new process is started for the same shards. Two flushers then read and flush the same shards, producing duplicate segments and leaking processes on each restart.

Strategy close() shuts down the factory-shared queue pool, so after a rebalance all messages are dropped and committed
The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and passed to every strategy from create_with_partitions. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown, shuts down the queues and joins the workers. Arroyo closes the strategy on every partition rebalance and then calls create_with_partitions again. The new strategy gets the same dead pool: the worker threads have exited and the queues are shut down. A later queue.put raises queue.ShutDown. submit() catches the exception, logs it, then marks the offset added and completed. The commit loop then commits those offsets, so every result after the first rebalance is silently skipped.
